findings.title: Threat inventory semantic corruption via duplicate finding IDs (no semantic validator)
findings.rationale: RT-THREAT-SEMANTIC-001 (TASK-1019) ESCALATED_BY_DESIGN: json.loads() accepts duplicate finding_id entries without error; no semantic validator for finding_id uniqueness, required fields, or status/evidence consistency exists. Implementation requires a new validator function that asserts finding_id uniqueness, required field completeness, and Mitigated requires non-null evidence_ref. regression_candidate=false per design (validator not yet implemented as of TASK-1019). Deferred because no v3.4 prompt is scoped to implement a standalone threat-findings semantic validator.

findings.title: Path dotdot normalization absent in classify_path() prefix matching
findings.rationale: RT-PATH-002 (TASK-1019) FAIL: classify_path() in workflow_constants.py does not normalize dotdot segments via os.path.normpath(). Path 'artifacts/code/../docs/orchestration.md' matches 'artifacts/code/' prefix literally and returns category 'code'; Codex CLI passes RACI check for a docs file (exit 0). Fix: add `normalized = os.path.normpath(normalized).replace('\\', '/')` to classify_path() before prefix matching. Deferred per TASK-1019 hardening_note; fix is small but requires regression test coverage and template sync before promotion.

findings.title: Symlink and realpath resolution absent in RACI path classification
findings.rationale: RT-SYMLINK-001 (TASK-1019) ESCALATED by design: classify_path() uses lexical prefix matching only; no os.path.realpath() resolution exists. A symlink or mirror path lexically under 'artifacts/code/' is classified as 'code' regardless of actual filesystem target, allowing category confusion. Fix requires realpath-aware audit policy at the filesystem boundary. Estimated complexity high because realpath resolution has platform-specific behavior and may require sandbox policy changes. Deferred to post-v3.4 scope.

findings.title: HITL attestation validator contract not implemented
findings.rationale: RT-HITL-ATTESTATION-001 (TASK-1019) FAIL: guard_status_validator.py does not parse or validate evidence_timestamp_source field in decision artifacts; reviewer_id presence alone passes nominal check; exit 1 observed only due to unrelated schema failures (missing '## Reasoning'), not HITL rejection. Implementation: guard_status_validator should (1) parse evidence_timestamp_source from decision artifact front matter, (2) reject values matching AI-authored narrative patterns (plain markdown text, Claude session output descriptions), (3) require timestamp source in allowed_sources: validator_json, command_stdout, file_mtime, git_commit, external_attestation, github_pr_review, issue_timestamp. Deferred because no v3.4 prompt is scoped to implement HITL attestation validation in guard_status_validator.
